buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  Iguaçu Falls, arid Atacama, the volcanic Galápagos Islands, and the mountains around Medellín are connected on one journey. Yet the physical demands vary between guided walks, altitude adjustment, a boat excursion, and a trip to Guatapé rock. The itinerary's principal off-road section actually takes place in Bolivia. We explain the activities, alternative island routes, and preparations for different conditions.
---

## Adventures across four countries: what the current itinerary includes

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [32-day route through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador, as well as Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. **Filtering for four countries does not create a ready-made trip limited to those four.** Read the entire itinerary, including days beyond this selection.

The trip combines guided walks, domestic flights, a boat excursion, and a high-altitude off-road journey. The [catalog for these four countries](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/) shows options without an interest restriction, while [multi-country adventures](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) can help compare other regions.

## Brazil: Iguaçu and an optional boat excursion

After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the route continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The principal group excursion on the Brazilian side of the falls follows maintained paths and viewpoints. It is an intensive nature walk, not an independent jungle trek.

**Macuco Safari** is listed as an optional paid activity. If you particularly want to go out on the water, arrange it separately, taking account of the following day, when travelers visit the Argentine side of the falls and fly to Buenos Aires. Do not assume that all activities around Iguaçu are included automatically.

## Chile: Atacama as preparation for the highlands

A sightseeing tour is planned in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop is intended for acclimatization before a two-day 4×4 journey across **Bolivia**, passing lagoons and geysers toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Parts of that high-altitude stage exceed 4,000 m.

The program does not promise a separate multi-day trek in Atacama. A telescope-based astronomy excursion is available for an additional charge and depends on the lunar cycle. For these days, a sensible pace, warm clothing for cold hours, and an assessment of how you feel at altitude are more important.

## Ecuador: two alternative routes for one boat day

A flight from Quito brings travelers to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Via Baltra, the group reaches [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and explores its highlands and lava tunnels. The itinerary then includes **one of two island options**:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas beaches. Seabirds, a coastal walk, and water activities within the confirmed itinerary are the main interests.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Punta Carrión. This combines a walk across a volcanic island with a marine excursion.

The precise option is selected after booking; this tour does not provide both on the same day. Visits to protected sites follow permitted routes and national park rules under the direction of an authorized guide. Bring protection from the sun and suitable boat clothing; sea conditions depend on actual weather.

## Colombia: mountain views without a promised ascent

After Ecuador, the journey visits [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the [replica of old El Peñol](/colombia/place/el-penol/), [El Peñón de Guatapé rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). This is a one-day excursion to local attractions and the surrounding reservoir. A separate sports climbing ascent is not listed as an included service.

City tours of Medellín, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) follow. Thus, the adventurous part of the Colombian stage primarily means exploring the mountains near Medellín rather than a trekking expedition. Those interested in architecture and history can use the [cultural selection for this country combination](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Exertion and preparation: four climates within an eight-country itinerary

Near Iguaçu, expect walks in a humid climate. Atacama is much drier, while the full itinerary subsequently climbs Bolivia's high plateau. The Galápagos add boat and island journeys. Colombian days alternate flights and city sightseeing. In practice, early starts and repeated hotel changes also demand stamina, so estimating the journey's difficulty only by walking distances would be misleading.

We help arrange optional activities, the island excursion alternative, and sensible connections. For the complete trip, entry and transit requirements must be checked according to travelers' citizenship, along with protected-area regulations and payment methods available in each country.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador

### Does the itinerary cover exactly four countries?

No. The [listed tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits eight countries over 32 days. The four named countries form a geography and theme filter.

### Is a multi-day Atacama hike included?

This itinerary includes a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama and preparation for the subsequent high-altitude section. No multi-day trekking in Chile is specified.

### Can North Seymour and South Plaza be visited on one day?

The tour includes one of these two alternatives. The islands to be visited are confirmed after booking.

### Is Macuco Safari an additional charge?

Yes. It is listed separately as a paid option. The main excursion on Iguaçu's Brazilian side is included.

lead: >-
  Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia provide four distinct introductions to South American history: Rio de Janeiro's landmarks, the capital city of Santiago, Quito's colonial art, Cartagena's fortified walls, and Bogotá's museums. On the current itinerary, these stops form part of an eight-country journey. We explain what is actually scheduled and where a historical excursion gives way to nature.
---

## A historical journey through Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the four selected main countries and a “Culture and History” focus. For example, the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. **The four countries in the filter represent an intersection of the route, not its full geography.** Choose by the program for every day, not simply the name of the selection.

Historical visits differ across the selected countries. Rio's attractions reflect the city's instantly recognizable image, Santiago tells the story of a capital, Quito offers colonial architecture, and Colombia spans several eras, from Cartagena's fortified port to Bogotá's pre-Columbian collections. [All routes for this combination](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/) and [multi-country cultural tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) let you compare without artificially shortening the journey.

## Brazil: two days exploring Rio de Janeiro

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary includes a trip to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, an excursion to Sugarloaf Mountain, and central landmarks including São Sebastião Cathedral. It is a good introduction for first-time visitors to Brazil, combining the city's famous panoramas with the guide's account of its history and modern life.

The route then visits [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The waterfalls are a nature-focused, rather than historical, stage, with an excursion on the Brazilian side. The trip subsequently continues through the Argentine side of Iguaçu, Buenos Aires, and Montevideo. These cities are part of the full eight-country product even though they are absent from this filter's title.

## Chile: from La Moneda to Santiago's urban history

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the program includes a tour with a Russian-speaking guide. The introduction begins at La Moneda Palace and Plaza de Armas, with the surrounding administrative and religious buildings. It continues to Santa Lucía Hill, overlooking the central city, and through the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes, and Providencia.

This creates a coherent story of Santiago in one sightseeing day: its historic center, government buildings, and modern architecture. An optional excursion to Maipo Valley wineries with wine tasting **costs extra** and is not a compulsory part of the cultural itinerary.

After Santiago, travelers fly to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This prepares for the high-altitude journey through Bolivia rather than extending Chile's city sightseeing.

## Ecuador: colonial Quito and landmarks at the equator

In Ecuador, the cultural heart of the journey is [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The itinerary includes a walk through its historic center, with squares, churches, monasteries, and architecture that combines European traditions with local artistic schools. Quito's historic center is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The sightseeing day also includes the equator line, Mitad del Mundo, and the Intiñan Museum.

This distinction matters: **Ecuador's cultural and historical program is concentrated in Quito**. Subsequent days on the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) focus on protected natural environments, lava tunnels, and boat excursions. The islands substantially extend the route, but should not be described as an archaeological tour.

## Colombia: Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary includes a city introduction and Comuna 13. Another day is devoted to Guatapé and El Peñón, where the main attractions are local settlements and scenery. A flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) follows.

Cartagena introduces travelers to a colonial port and the Caribbean coast's military architecture. The city tour visits historic streets, fortifications, and San Felipe de Barajas Fortress. Its fortifications and historic ensemble are on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the experience changes again: La Candelaria's historic quarter, the Gold Museum, Botero Collection, and city squares. The excursion ends with views from Monserrate. Another day is dedicated to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. When planning the Bogotá visit, observe the museum closures specified in the itinerary: the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Mint Museum and Botero Collection close on Tuesdays.

## Why the cultural theme extends beyond these four countries

The full 32-day journey includes major historical sites not named in the geographic filter: Tiwanaku in Bolivia, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) in Peru, and excursions around Buenos Aires and Montevideo. This is another reason to read the [entire route program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) before making a choice.

The historical content spans colonial quarters, Inca heritage, archaeological monuments, and contemporary urban art. The duration and transfers between them are defined by specific excursion days. Ada Tours can discuss the journey's emphasis and preferred museums while preserving the arrangements for transfers and domestic flights.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural journeys through Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia

### Is there a separate tour limited to these four countries?

This selection features the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) through eight countries. Four countries are used as a filter and do not constitute a separate shortened itinerary.

### Where does the route offer the most colonial architecture?

In the selected geography, Quito's historic center and Cartagena's fortified city stand out. Santiago and Bogotá also include tours of historic districts and monuments.

### Are the Galápagos included in the cultural section?

The islands belong to the full Ecuador itinerary, but their principal activities are wildlife watching, lava tunnels, and a boat excursion. For wildlife-focused choices, see the [“Wildlife and Safari” selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/interests/wildlife/).

### Can I devote more time to Bogotá's museums?

The itinerary and possible adjustments can be discussed when planning, taking account of museum closure days, flights, and the following day's excursion to Zipaquirá.

kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Nature in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  Iguaçu Falls in Brazil, the mountains and arid valleys of northern Chile, El Peñón rock near Guatapé in Colombia, and the ecosystems of Ecuador's Galápagos all feature in a single 32-day journey through South America. Nature appears in different forms at each stage. We explain where dedicated excursions are planned, where there is only a transfer, and why the boat day's alternative routes matter.
---

## Four natural worlds within one extended journey

In [Brazil](/brazil/), the route connects Rio's granite mountains with Iguaçu Falls. In [Chile](/chile/), travelers fly to Calama, travel to San Pedro de Atacama, and begin the high-altitude section of the next country. In [Colombia](/colombia/), there is an excursion to El Peñón and the Guatapé reservoir. In [Ecuador](/ecuador/), the route takes in a remarkable natural region, the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is the [32-day trip through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Beyond the four selected countries, it visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. These nature-focused stages should therefore be assessed **in the context of the whole tour**, including flights and border crossings.

| Country | Principal natural sights |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Iguaçu and Rio's mountains |
| Chile | Atacama and the route toward the Andes |
| Colombia | El Peñón, Guatapé |
| Ecuador | Galápagos Islands |

This page compares **four different nature stages of one program**. For other combinations, explore the [multi-country nature tour catalog](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Brazil: from Corcovado to mighty waterfalls

The early days pass through São Paulo and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The city has remarkable topography: forested mountain slopes rise directly above urban neighborhoods, and Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain offer views over the bay.

The group then flies to [Iguaçu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side offers broad panoramas of the cascades, while the Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú offers views from a different network of paths. UNESCO lists Brazil's Iguaçu National Park as natural World Heritage for its waterfalls and surviving Atlantic Forest.

**Both sides** are included in the itinerary, but on separate days, with border procedures between them. Heavy rain can affect access to trails. To visit the main viewpoints, account for transfers, park entry, and the onward flight to Buenos Aires.

## Chile: the nature stage begins after Santiago

Following city visits in Argentina, travelers arrive in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) are then scheduled. This journey crosses the dry north, known for striking landforms and volcanic mountains.

Read the program precisely: **the nighttime astronomy excursion in Atacama is optional**, not a required part of the basic sightseeing day. The main stop in San Pedro also helps prepare for the next high-altitude section.

Only after the Chilean border does the two-day jeep itinerary across lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat begin **in Bolivia**. Those colorful highland lagoons should not be attributed to Chile simply because the trip starts from San Pedro. Geographic accuracy matters for assessing the time spent in each country.

## Colombia: Guatapé and El Peñón rock

After Ecuador, the group arrives in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The next day includes an eight-hour excursion to the [El Peñol](/colombia/place/el-penol/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) area. A massive rock monolith rises above green hills and a reservoir. This setting differs dramatically from the dry Atacama and the humid forest of Iguaçu.

The excursion combines natural viewpoints with Guatapé's colorful houses. Later Colombian days include Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá, and Zipaquirá, where much of the itinerary concerns cities and cultural attractions.

Thus, **Colombia's dedicated nature day is El Peñón and Guatapé**. Hikes through national parks or sightings of rare animals in other cities should not be promised automatically; those excursions would have to be listed separately.

## Ecuador: how the Galápagos boat day works

After arriving in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), travelers continue to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The group lands on Baltra, crosses the Itabaca Channel to Santa Cruz, and then travels to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). The island landscape shifts from dry areas to greener zones.

The program has a separate boat day with **two alternatives**. The first is North Seymour and Bachas; the second is South Plaza and Punta Carrión. One route is selected and confirmed after booking, rather than visiting all four sites.

The nature theme is most evident here: ocean, volcanic shores, native birds, and other wildlife. Sightings of specific species at specific times are not guaranteed. The Galápagos National Park Directorate oversees marine and terrestrial visitor sites and authorized activities, so the availability of any route is determined by conservation rules.

After the islands, the route continues through Guayaquil to Colombia. The Galápagos have their own dedicated stage, but this is **not a multi-week expedition across the entire archipelago**.

## Preparing luggage, dates, and connections

One itinerary combines Brazil's hot humid regions, dry high-altitude conditions beyond northern Chile, a mountain day in Colombia, and boat excursions in Ecuador. At Iguaçu, bring rain protection and shoes with non-slip soles; in the Andes, warm clothing and sun protection; in the Galápagos, clothing suitable for landings and compliant with conservation regulations.

The chief logistical feature is the large number of flights and border crossings. The boat excursion must be confirmed according to the island route, while the highland section after San Pedro requires attention to acclimatization. We help create a workable travel sequence and check exactly which nature excursions are included.

Documents must cover **all eight countries** and transit airports. Requirements depend on citizenship, the route, and current rules; the entry conditions of one country cannot be applied to the others.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador

### Can all four island attractions be visited in one day?

On this tour the boat day offers alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas **or** South Plaza with Punta Carrión. One option is confirmed, not both.

### Are Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons included in Chile?

No. The Altiplano lagoons and Uyuni are visited within Bolivia. Chile's stage includes Santiago and the trip to San Pedro de Atacama before that section begins.

### Are Galápagos wildlife sightings guaranteed?

No. The Galápagos are known for their rich island wildlife, but sightings depend on conditions and the permitted route. Visits are regulated by the national park.

## Nature in four countries: where wildlife is actually observed

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador as main countries under the “Wildlife and Safari” theme. The reason for this label is the included wildlife-watching activities in the Galápagos. The [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. **A four-country filter does not shorten the actual route.** The main nature experiences within the selected geography are concentrated around [Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

Including a country in a themed selection does not mean rare wildlife is observed there every day. The Chilean stage focuses on a flight and acclimatization; Colombia mainly combines cities with the excursion to Guatapé. [All itineraries for this combination](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/) are available separately, while trips focused on animals in other regions appear in the [multi-country “Wildlife and Safari” catalog](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). For waterfalls, mountains, and desert landscapes, see [the same country combination under “Nature”](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia_ecuador/interests/nature/).

## Brazil: waterfalls and the humid forest of Iguaçu

After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travelers reach [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The main excursion follows paths and viewpoints on the Brazilian side of the falls. The humid forest, river, and multiple cascades are natural attractions in their own right.

**The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are available as paid extras.** They should not be automatically included in the tour price or described as compulsory. Macuco Safari is a boat trip toward the falls: the word “safari” here does not mean dedicated wildlife watching. Even if a visit focused on birds is added, encountering any particular species in the wild cannot be guaranteed. The next day includes the Argentine side of Iguaçu and a flight to Buenos Aires, so free time is limited by the itinerary.

## Chile: Atacama as a change of natural environment

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), travelers explore the city before flying to Calama and driving to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The scenery shifts from tropical to arid, with volcanic peaks and open valleys.

However, the precise itinerary allocates the Chilean day to **travel and acclimatization** before Bolivia's jeep journey. It does not include a specialist safari, a search for flamingos, or a separate nature-reserve hike in Chile. The high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) lie in the next country on the complete route. A nighttime astronomy excursion in Atacama can be arranged at additional cost, but it involves observing the sky, not animals.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos Islands and wild animals

After the historical excursion in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the program continues by air to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Via Baltra, visitors reach [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), with its highlands, lava tunnels, and Puerto Ayora.

The separate boat day offers **two mutually exclusive included alternatives**:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas beaches. During coastal walks, visitors may encounter blue-footed boobies, frigatebirds, sea lions, and other archipelago wildlife. The marine section may include swimming and snorkeling within the confirmed itinerary.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Punta Carrión. Another island walk offers sea lions, land iguanas, birds, volcanic shores, and travel by boat.

**We do not promise both island routes on the same day.** One branch is confirmed after booking. The list of animals describes possible sightings, not a guarantee that they will appear: these are wild animals whose presence depends on season and behavior.

## Rules for observing wildlife

The Galápagos are protected for their exceptional natural value. Visitors must stay on permitted trails, follow instructions from an authorized guide, and keep a safe distance from animals. Do not feed seabirds or sea lions, touch iguanas for photographs, or leave litter.

For the boat excursion, bring footwear for rocky shores, sun protection, and suitable clothing, and be prepared for changes in the weather. Seeing animals in their natural habitat without disturbing them matters more than getting close for a photograph. The actual availability of snorkeling and landings must be checked against the confirmed island option.

## Colombia: Guatapé mountain scenery and city tours

The itinerary continues from Ecuador to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), then to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), [El Peñón rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), and the reservoir. This offers a look at mountainous Colombian scenery and local settlements. **The program contains no organized birdwatching or safari in Colombia.**

The following days are devoted to Comuna 13, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), and Zipaquirá. The content is mainly cultural. This alternation is natural on an extended journey, but when choosing a wildlife-focused tour, distinguish nature excursions from city visits.

## Choosing the trip's main nature experience

For seabirds, iguanas, and sea lions, the first priority is to discuss **the Galápagos island excursion alternative** with Ada Tours. Iguaçu is suited to waterfall and humid-forest scenery, Atacama to desert landscapes, and Guatapé to mountain panoramas. The remainder of the eight-country route adds Andean plateaus, historical cities, and flights.

Before traveling, check seasonal and weather restrictions, permit requirements, boat-excursion arrangements, and optional service inclusions. The tour lasts 32 days, so practical comfort depends not just on wildlife encounters but also on the number of transfers.

## Frequently asked questions about animals and nature in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador

### Can blue-footed boobies be guaranteed?

No. They are characteristic of the Galápagos and mentioned in the itinerary, but sightings depend on natural conditions.

### Are North Seymour and South Plaza visited on one day?

No. **One of two alternatives** is included. The specific route is confirmed after booking.

### Is the Iguaçu Bird Park part of the main tour?

No. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are paid optional activities.

### Is there a safari in the Colombian section?

The selected tour includes an excursion to Guatapé and city sightseeing. There is no separate safari or rare-wildlife-watching activity in Colombia.

## Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Colombia: what the itinerary includes

These four countries connect Brazil's oceanfront cities, Chile's dry highlands, Peru's historical monuments, and widely differing parts of Colombia, from the Andes to the Caribbean coast. However, we offer this combination **as part of a single extended tour, not as a stand-alone itinerary limited to four countries**.

The [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) starts in Brazil. Travelers then visit Argentina and Uruguay, fly to Chile, continue through Bolivia into Peru, travel through Ecuador and the Galápagos, and finish in Colombia. The absence of Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Ecuador from this selection's title **does not remove them from the actual program or its price**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If you want to visit only Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Colombia, international flights, city order, dates of attraction visits, and the budget will need to be arranged from scratch. The price of the complete 32-day tour is not the price of a shortened journey.

## Brazil: Rio de Janeiro and Iguaçu Falls

The journey starts in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) and continues to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The program includes excursions to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. The group then flies to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) to visit the Brazilian side of the waterfalls.

This combines city and nature experiences with walks, viewpoints, and humid tropical weather. Rain can affect visibility from Rio's hills, while spray is common around the falls. Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and protection for electronic equipment against moisture are sufficient for these early days.

After Brazil, the tour visits the Argentine side of Iguaçu, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), and Montevideo. Only then does the group fly to Chile. There is no direct transfer from Iguaçu to Santiago on this itinerary. Other geographic options can be compared in the [Brazil tours catalog](/brazil/tour/).

## Chile: from Santiago to the Atacama Desert

Chile's stage begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). After a sightseeing tour, the group flies to Calama and transfers to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A nighttime astronomy excursion is offered separately; it must not be assumed to be included in the price.

The journey continues from Atacama **through Bolivia**, rather than by direct flight into Peru. In off-road vehicles, the group crosses high-altitude lagoons, geothermal areas, and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), then travels to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). Via Tiwanaku and a border crossing, the route reaches Puno in Peru.

This stage requires particular preparation. Temperatures and altitudes change, and some sections exceed 4,000 m. Medical consultation before departure is especially important for travelers with chronic conditions or previous altitude-related difficulties. Check insurance coverage, bring warm clothes, and allow time to acclimatize. The Bolivian section lasts several days: replacing it with a direct flight would change both the substance and the cost of the entire itinerary.

For a trip focused on Chile alone, [other tours in the country](/chile/tour/) offer different regions and levels of exertion.

## Peru: from Titicaca to Machu Picchu

The group enters Peru from the south. The itinerary includes [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), followed by a tourist bus with sightseeing stops to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). A separate day is dedicated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), with a train journey, a guided visit, and a return to Cusco.

For Machu Picchu, book admission for a specific day, time, and visiting route in advance. When tailoring a shorter journey, it makes sense to secure the archaeological site's entry first and then arrange transfers and flights. Otherwise, a convenient flight may coincide with the chosen Machu Picchu circuit being unavailable.

Historic sights in Cusco and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) for city sightseeing follow. Physical demands differ from those of an itinerary that begins with a direct flight to Peru's capital: by this point, travelers have already completed Bolivia's highland section. Compare further programs in the [Peru tours catalog](/peru/tour/).

## Ecuador and the Galápagos lie between Peru and Colombia

After Lima, the current tour travels to Quito and then to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The program includes [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and one of two alternative boat excursions. After the islands, travelers return to the mainland via [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/) and fly to Colombia.

Ecuador is a full multi-day stage on this route. Flights to the islands, biosecurity rules, and the required TCT Transit Control Card entail their own preparations. **Travel between Peru and Colombia must not be treated as an ordinary connection.**

A tailored itinerary limited to the four selected countries requires a meaningful choice: retain the Galápagos as an additional major experience or arrange a direct flight from Peru to Colombia. The decision changes both duration and the complete transport plan.

## Colombia: Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá

The final stage begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), with an excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and a visit to Comuna 13. A flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) on the Caribbean coast follows. The journey ends in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), with museums, Monserrate, and an excursion to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Cartagena is hot and humid, while high-altitude Bogotá feels noticeably cooler. The same luggage already containing warm clothes for Atacama and Cusco needs room for lightweight items. The program uses domestic flights within Colombia, so baggage restrictions must be checked for every stage.

When shortening the trip, first decide whether to retain all three cities. Choosing just one or two Colombian centers changes the sightseeing and flight arrangements. [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) provide alternatives to compare.

## Documents, money, and connections across eight countries

The four named countries have their own entry rules. However, **our actual itinerary covers eight nations**. For instance, a one-day trip to Uruguay involves exiting Argentina and returning to it, while the journey from Chile to Peru passes through Bolivia. Check documents for the real sequence of borders according to each traveler's citizenship and passport type, including transit and potential re-entry requirements.

| Stage | Principal preparation |
|---|---|
| Brazil and Argentina | Both sides of Iguaçu |
| Chile and Bolivia | Altitude and land border |
| Peru | Timed entry to Machu Picchu |
| Ecuador | Galápagos, TCT, and baggage |
| Colombia | Domestic flights |

The Brazilian real (BRL), Chilean peso (CLP), Peruvian sol (PEN), and Colombian peso (COP) are the currencies of the four named countries. The actual itinerary also calls for payment arrangements in Argentina, Uruguay, and Bolivia, while Ecuador uses the US dollar. Whether foreign or Russian bank cards work, what fees apply, how cash is withdrawn, and what backup payment methods are available depend on the country and issuing bank. No single payment method is guaranteed across all eight countries.

Our full itinerary includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, and a defined selection of excursions. The international flight to the starting point is paid separately. See the detailed terms in the [32-day tour description](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/); any shortened version must be priced afresh.

## Choosing when you have less time

If Machu Picchu and the Inca cities are your principal goals, structure the calendar around the Peruvian section. To experience desert scenery and mountain roads, preserve the Atacama stage and allow time for acclimatization. Travelers more interested in Rio and Colombian cities can discuss a different international-flight route without the full high-altitude section in Bolivia.

We help coordinate destinations, flights, accommodation, and excursions to suit the selected duration. Other combinations can be explored on the [multi-country travel page](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Peru

### Can I book a ready-made tour limited to these four countries?

This selection features a 32-day journey through eight countries. A trip restricted to Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Colombia needs a tailored itinerary and separate pricing.

### Can I travel directly from Atacama to Peru?

Different transport can be discussed for a tailored program. The published tour connects Chile and Peru via Bolivia's lagoons, Uyuni, and La Paz.

### Are the Galápagos Islands included?

Yes. The full eight-country itinerary includes Ecuador and the Galápagos. The islands are not automatically part of a trip limited to the four countries in the title.

### Where does the journey end?

The final stage of the current tour passes through Medellín, Cartagena, and Bogotá, after which the program provides for a return to São Paulo.
